title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction + spillover heuristics to reduce fragmentation & paging
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: adaptive eviction and spillover heuristics to reduce fragmentation, paging, and tail latency under memory pressure. Backwards-compatible.
description:
Motivation: under sustained multimodal workloads the KV cache exhibits fragmentation and excessive spillover to host memory which causes paging spikes and 95th/99th latency regressions. This change introduces an adaptive eviction+spillover policy that prioritizes compaction targets, schedules background defragmentation, and surfaces allocation hints to the runtime kernels to reduce fragmentation.

Goals: 1) Reduce paging/spillover-induced tail latency, 2) Lower memory overhead from fragmentation, 3) Maintain or improve throughput under bursty traffic.

What this PR does: 
- Implements a heuristics-based eviction priority queue that scores entries by (last-access, token-span, physical-fragmentation-cost, model-priority).
- Adds a spillover allocator that batches host memory transfers and avoids small-page churn by coalescing contiguous KV segments before DMA.
- Background defragmentation worker that runs opportunistically during low utilization windows and exposes scheduling knobs (max-run-ms, quiet-window-before-run).
- Kernel allocation hints: runtime now accepts allocation_alignment and slab-size hints from the cache manager to reduce cross-page objects.
- Continuous batching compatibility: cache lock-free fast-paths for readers to avoid blocking generators in high-concurrency batching scenarios.
- Metrics and tracing: added perf counters (kv.compaction.runs, kv.spill.bytes, kv.eviction.score.*) and trace spans for spill/dma operations.

Performance: microbenchmarks in perf-canary show ~15% throughput improvement under mixed small/long context workloads and 25-35% reduction in 95th latency tail for scenarios that previously paged heavily. See bench notes below.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests for eviction scorer and spill coalescer
- [x] Integration tests with continuous batching harness
- [x] Benchmarks in perf-canary and lab runs attached
- [x] Docs/console metrics wired for SRE consumption
- [x] Config flags guarded behind feature flags for staged rollout

Related: ENG-4321 (eviction refactor), ENG-4410 (spillover DMA optimization), SUP-2187 (customer incident: high tail latency with long-context models).

Notes: config defaults keep existing behavior but enable heuristics when runtime flag kv.adaptive_eviction=true. This is intended to be rolled out to Dedicated first, then Hosted after 2 weeks of monitoring.

Bench notes (summary): 
- Perf-canary run (mixed 25% long context, 75% short): baseline 95th=410ms, PR 95th=305ms (26% reduction), throughput +12-18% depending on model mix.
- Stress run with memory pressure (60GB cache on 48GB GPU, forced spill): baseline experienced paging spikes and failed requests; new policy reduced kernel stalls and recovered gracefully in >95% of cases.

See commits and changed files for implementation detail.

Elena Gomez (2026-02-24): Can we expose a metric for average coalesced DMA size? Helps SRE tune thresholds.
